blocks.prompt: 3. Find a point on the curve \(x + y - e^{y} = 0\) where the tangent line is vertical. Also, find the equations of the tangent and normal at that point.
blocks.explanation:
Yahan curve implicit shakal mein hai (\(y\) alag se likha hua nahi), is liye implicit differentiation lagegi.
Diya kya hai? Curve \(x + y - e^{y} = 0\).
Find kya karna hai? Woh point jahan tangent khari (vertical) ho, aur wahan tangent aur normal.
Rule kaunsa? Vertical tangent par \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) be-hadd bara (\(\pm\infty\)) hota hai, yani us ka denominator zero.
Plan: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) nikalo, denominator zero karo, point nikalo; tangent \(x = x_0\), normal \(y = y_0\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(x + y - e^{y} = 0\) ...(1).
Maloom karna: woh point jahan tangent vertical hai, aur wahan tangent aur normal.
Tareeqa: (1) ko implicit differentiate karenge. Vertical tangent ka slope \(m = \pm\infty\) hai, yani \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) ka denominator zero ho aur numerator zero na ho.

(1) ko \(x\) ke lehaz se differentiate karein
\[1 + \dfrac{dy}{dx} - e^{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\]
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx}(1 - e^{y}) = -1\]
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{e^{y} - 1}\]
Kyun: \(x\) ka derivative 1, \(y\) ka derivative \(\frac{dy}{dx}\). \(y\) khud \(x\) ka function hai, is liye \(\frac{d}{dx}e^{y} = e^{y}\frac{dy}{dx}\) (chain rule). Phir \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) wali terms ikatthi kar ke common nikala, aur upar neeche \(-1\) se multiply kar ke saaf shakal banayi.
Dhyan dein: \(e^{y}\) ka derivative sirf \(e^{y}\) likh dena ghalat hai; \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) saath lagana zaroori hai.

Slope kahan be-hadd hai?
\[e^{y} - 1 = 0 \Rightarrow e^{y} = 1\]
\[y = 0\]
Kyun: numerator 1 hai jo kabhi zero nahi hota, to \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) theek wahan be-hadd bara hoga jahan denominator zero ho. \(e^{y} = 1\) sirf \(y = 0\) par hota hai, kyunke \(e^{0} = 1\).

Point nikalein
(1) mein \(y = 0\) rakhein:
\[x + 0 - e^{0} = 0 \Rightarrow x = 1\]
Point \((1, 0)\) hai.
Kyun: point curve par hona chahiye, is liye \(y = 0\) ko asal equation mein rakh kar \(x\) nikala.

Tangent aur normal
Tangent (point \((1, 0)\) se khari line):
\[x = 1\]
Normal (point \((1, 0)\) se leti hui line):
\[y = 0\]
Kyun: vertical tangent hamesha \(x = x_0\) hoti hai. Normal us par perpendicular hai, aur khari line par perpendicular leti hui line hoti hai: \(y = y_0\), yani yahan \(x\)-axis.

Tasdeeq
\((1, 0)\) ko (1) mein rakhein: \(1 + 0 - 1 = 0\), theek. Ek aur nazar: (1) se \(x = e^{y} - y\), to \(\frac{dx}{dy} = e^{y} - 1\), jo \(y = 0\) par zero hai. Matlab us point par \(y\) badalne se \(x\) nahi badalta, curve wahan seedha upar neeche ja raha hai. Yahi vertical tangent hai.
